title: Background Refetching
description: Control background refetching behavior to keep data fresh without disrupting the user experience.

data.text: React Query can automatically refetch data in the background when certain events occur: the window regains focus, the network reconnects, or a timer interval elapses. These behaviors keep data fresh without user intervention, but they can also cause unnecessary requests if misconfigured.

items: refetchOnWindowFocus: Refetch when user switches back to the tab.
refetchOnReconnect: Refetch when network comes back online.
refetchOnMount: Refetch when a new component mounts.
refetchInterval: Poll at a fixed interval in milliseconds.
data.title: Triggers
Configuring refetch behavior

data.text: For data that does not need to be fresh, disable background refetching to reduce server load. Use this for static content, documentation pages, or data that updates on explicit user action.
Disable `refetchOnWindowFocus` for forms or multi-step wizards. Accidental refetches during input can be frustrating for users.
data.title: User Experience
Background Refetching Key Points
points: Background refetching keeps data fresh automatically.
Window focus and reconnect are the most common triggers.
Use polling with refetchInterval for near-real-time data.
Disable refetching for static or user-input-heavy pages.
data.takeaway: Background refetching is a powerful default, but should be tuned per use case.
